newsitem.title: HAITI: Cement workers block road in Haiti protest.
newsitem.headline: Cement workers block road in Haiti protest.

text.p: Haitian workers who lost their jobs when the state cement factory closed in 1992 erected barricades of wrecked cars and burning tires across a main highway in a protest on Monday.
Traffic backed up for 30 miles (50 km) for several hours until riot police cleared the demonstration.
The factory closed in 1992 and workers said they were owed back pay and unable to feed their families.
"The government must negotiate with us," protest leader Ronald Dirigets said.

Ciment d'Haiti, the state-run cement factory, is unlikely to reopen until the government completes plans for its privatisation. Considered a money-loser when it was in operation, it will be open to bids by foreign contractors who workers fear will not hire as many Haitians.

The cement factory and others in the area were closed during a U.S.-imposed embargo called in reaction to a 1991 military coup. Under the embargo, unemployment soared to its current level of 70 percent.
In the afternoon, black-uniformed riot police carrying shields and batons pushed protesters off the road and tore down the road blocks by using bulldozers.

"The government has forgotten that we exist. This area was once prosperous with several companies to employ people. Now there is nothing. We will not vote for these people again because life just gets worse and worse," protester Joseph Manuel said.
